subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-inject SKILL.md content when skill is invoked via slash command

question: Should explicit non-tool skill slash invocations deterministically inject SKILL.md into model context, and what trust/authority boundary should govern that injected content?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing whether SKILL.md becomes guaranteed model context affects prompt authority, untrusted skill handling, and session/context semantics in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Define Trust Contract Then Implement
options.body: Set the SKILL.md authority and isolation rules first, then add deterministic slash-invocation loading through the shared skill command path.

options.title: Keep Advisory Default
options.body: Leave non-tool skill slash invocations as model-routed requests and require `command-dispatch: tool` for deterministic behavior.

options.title: Defer To Broader Skill Contract Work
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the broader instruction-isolation or native/Codex skill-contract decisions before implementation.

recommendation.title: Define Trust Contract Then Implement
recommendation.body: Set the SKILL.md authority and isolation rules first, then add deterministic slash-invocation loading through the shared skill command path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the current user-invocable skill command behavior and owns the overlapping local skill routing proposal.
